title: Zephyr eCommerce POC - stress sweep report (throughput, latency, cost)
summary: This working report captures the stress sweep results run for Zephyr eCommerce (search + personalized recommendations endpoint). Goal was to understand the operational throughput envelope, p95 latency under load, and per-1M-token cost implications across model variants and deployment configs. Tests run on Dedicated pools (A100x2 and H100x4 flavors) and Hosted fallback routing. Key takeaway: rw-7b-opt with 4-sample batching on H100 yields best dollars-per-query at p95 ~120ms for short-chat flows; larger-ctx recommendation flows benefit from kv-cache sharing and CPU-level prefiltering to keep cost predictable.
objective: Deliver concrete numbers to Zephyr engineering/product for: 1) SLA feasibility for 99% of user queries under peak shopping traffic, 2) recommended Dedicated config (instance type + pool size), 3) deployment knobs (batching, cache TTL, quantization) to meet cost targets (<= $0.015 per 1k tokens for recommendations).
scope_and_constraints: Scope: search-autocomplete (prompt tokens ~20–60), recommendation-render (prompt tokens ~120–600), small chat/assistant (prompt tokens ~40–200). Excluded: multi-turn conversational reranking, embeddings workloads. Tests simulated user arrival patterns based on Zephyr traffic sample (weekend peak) supplied as synthetic trace. Constraint: private data redaction enforced, so input prompts were sanitized; cost numbers are runtime-only and exclude storage/transfer and Dedicated reservation amortization.
test_matrix_and_configs: Matrix rows: model variant (rw-7b-opt, rw-13b-static, rw-3b-q4), precision (fp16, int8 quant), routing (dedicated-A100, dedicated-H100, hosted), batch_size targets (1, 4, 8, 16 for short ctx; 1,2,4 for long ctx), kv_cache (disabled, enabled shared), autoscale_policy (none, scale-by-cpu, scale-by-latency). Each test ran for 15 minutes steady-state after warmup; 3 repeats per cell. Synthetic traces: baseline (200 RPS steady, 99th percentile arrival bursts 2x), peak (800 RPS bursts up to 3x), flash (2000 RPS short spikes for 60s).
hardware_and_software_environment: Dedicated pools provisioned via Redwood Dedicated: - A100x2 nodes (40GB GPU) - H100x4 nodes (640GB aggregate GPU) Runtime: Redwood serving runtime v2.8.3, kernel profile set 'prod-low-latency'. Model builds from model-catalog: rw-3b-q4 (4-bit quantized), rw-7b-opt (native fp16 optimized), rw-13b-static (fp16 static build). Autoscale policy: min 1 node, max 10 nodes. Metrics captured from Redwood Console (per-token cost, per-route latency histograms) and node-level GPU util via Prometheus exporters.
methodology: 1) Warmup: 5 minutes at 50% baseline RPS to populate kv caches and JIT kernels. 2) Sweep: for each cell, ramp from 0 to target RPS in 30s, maintain for 15min, capture latency histograms, tail latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, and cost breakdowns. 3) Repeats: 3 runs; report median of medians and max of p95 across repeats. 4) Load shaping used closed-loop to preserve realistic concurrency profiles (arrival distributions derived from Zephyr sample). 5) Cost calc: token costs from Redwood metering (inference compute + memory overhead per node), normalized to per-1k-token and per-query given median output lengths.
results:
Key aggregated numbers (median across repeats):
- Search-autocomplete (short ctx ~30 tokens): rw-7b-opt @ H100, batch=4 -> throughput 1200 QPS, p50=18ms, p95=78ms, gpu_util=62%, cost = $0.0075 per 1k tokens.
- Search-autocomplete @ A100, batch=4 -> throughput 880 QPS, p95=120ms, cost = $0.0098 per 1k tokens.
- Recommendation (long ctx ~320 tokens): rw-13b-static @ H100, batch=1, kv_cache enabled -> throughput 85 QPS, p95=310ms, cost = $0.045 per 1k tokens.
- Recommendation @ rw-7b-opt fp16 with kv-cache and prefiltering -> throughput 140 QPS, p95=190ms, cost = $0.023 per 1k tokens.
- rw-3b-q4 int8 (cheap variant) for short ctx: throughput 900 QPS, p95=110ms, cost = $0.0042 per 1k tokens but with ~6% token-level quality drift on BLEU-like automatic metric used for initial quality check.
- Hosted fallback: during capacity saturation (simulated 2x burst) latency p95 jumped to 1.2s for long ctx flows; cost per 1k tokens elevated by ~15% due to multi-region egress and fallback model selection.
analysis: 1) H100 advantages: systematic lower p95 and improved throughput for fp16 models; yields best cost/perf for heavy query workloads despite higher per-hour cost because of better consolidation. 2) Batch sizing: short ctx benefits from batch 4–8; beyond 8 marginal latency improvements but throughput plateau due to tokenization overhead. 3) kv-cache: crucial for recommendation workloads where large repeated context occurs; enabling shared kv-cache reduced compute by ~28% and p95 by ~22% on long ctx. 4) Quantized 3b: strong cost win for non-critical quality endpoints (search suggestions) but not recommended for ranking/recommendations without retraining calibration. 5) Autoscale: scale-by-latency policy produced fewer tail events than cpu-based scaling under flash bursts because of better preservation of in-flight batch completion times.
recommendations:
Short term (POC -> pilot):
- Provision Dedicated H100 pool sized to sustain 2x baseline for search flows: start with 4 H100 nodes dedicated to search-autocomplete with batch target 4 and kernel profile 'prod-low-latency'.
- Route recommendation-render to mixed pool: rw-13b-static for high-quality long-ctx returns, and rw-7b-opt as a lower-cost fallback; enable kv-cache with TTL 10 minutes and cache sharding per customer segment.
- Use rw-3b-q4 for ephemeral suggestion endpoints where quality tolerance exists; add periodic offline evals to detect drift.

Operational knobs:
- Set autoscale to 'scale-by-latency' with warmup 30s, cool-down 90s.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for sessions with >2 repeated queries within 10m.
- Apply model pinning for checkout-critical flows to prevent unexpected model rollouts.

Cost guidance:
- Expected incremental Dedicated cost (operational compute) for pilot ~ $22k/month for the above pool; amortized per-1M tokens in steady baseline ~ $X.Y (detailed cost spreadsheet linked).
risks_and_unknowns:
- Quality vs quantization: automatic metric shows 6% drop for rw-3b-q4; need human eval on top queries.
- Traffic pattern accuracy: tests were driven by synthetic trace based on Zephyr sample, but real-world burstiness (promo events) may be higher. Recommend running production canary during next sale.
- Reservation amortization: Dedicated estimates here exclude multi-month reservation discounts; finance needs to model committed spend to present full TCO.
- Network egress: cross-region fallback increases tail and cost; if Zephyr plans multi-region user base, recommend local Dedicated pools or edge routing.

notes_and_observations:
- During one H100 run we observed a kernel fallback for rw-13b-static causing a ~40ms spike at 95th percentile; traced to an NMS memory allocation pattern, filed GHPR linked above.
- Prefiltering (lightweight CPU-side filter to reject irrelevant recommendation candidates) reduced downstream GPU work by ~12% and was easy to instrument.
- Zephyr asked about single-tenant vs multi-tenant: single-tenant pools reduce noisy neighbor risk and give more predictable p95 but increase cost; recommended hybrid approach (critical checkout model single-tenant, suggestions multi-tenant).
author_notes: This doc is a working artifact for Zephyr POC. Numbers are median/typical from our runs in June and should be treated as directional for architecture decisions. Please ping author for raw csvs or to re-run any cell with different tails or larger sample sizes.
